recognize_zh: 切片中瀰漫片狀的漿細胞（核偏心、車輪狀染色質、部分有核仁或雙核），細胞之間夾著長條狀、均質粉紅色的桿狀結晶，另有較小的針狀結晶位於細胞胞質內，符合伴隨結晶沉積的漿細胞骨髓瘤。
features: Diffuse sheets of plasma cells with eccentric round nuclei, clock-face chromatin and moderate amphophilic cytoplasm
Occasional binucleate plasma cells, visible nucleoli and a mitotic figure
Large extracellular elongated rectangular, homogeneous eosinophilic crystals lying between tumor cells
Smaller needle/spindle-shaped eosinophilic crystals within plasma cell cytoplasm (panel B)
Scattered small hexagonal eosinophilic structures and a few interspersed stromal cells
describe_en: Biopsy section shows a diffuse sheet-like infiltrate of plasma cells with eccentric nuclei, coarse clock-face chromatin, occasional nucleoli, binucleate forms and mitoses. Large, elongated rod-shaped homogeneous eosinophilic crystals are present extracellularly between tumor cells, and smaller needle-like crystals are seen within the cytoplasm of some plasma cells. No crystal-laden histiocyte aggregates are evident on this image. Findings are consistent with plasma cell myeloma with extracellular and intracellular immunoglobulin crystal deposition; CD138 and kappa/lambda staining of the tumor and crystals, and evaluation of renal function for light chain crystalline nephropathy, are recommended.

ddx.vs: In CSH the crystals are packed within CD68+/CD163+ histiocytes with abundant cytoplasm rather than lying free between and within CD138+ plasma cells.
Charcot-Leyden crystals are slender bipyramidal crystals associated with eosinophils and are galectin-10 positive, not immunoglobulin light chain.
These have abundant fibrillary 'crumpled tissue paper' cytoplasm in histiocytes rather than discrete rigid rod-shaped crystals.
